title: Another Dravid in India Colours. Rahul's Younger Son Anvay Gets His First National Call-Up.
excerpt: The 15-year-old wicketkeeper-batter from Karnataka has been named in India's U-19 squad for the Sri Lanka tour starting July 4.
body:
Rahul Dravid's younger son, Anvay, has been named in India's Under-19 squad for the tour of Sri Lanka in July — his first call-up to a national age-group side.

The BCCI's Junior Cricket Committee announced the squads on Wednesday for a tour comprising three Youth ODIs and two Youth Tests, to be played between July 4 and 23. Anvay, a wicketkeeper-batter who has impressed in Karnataka U-16 cricket, was included in the one-day squad alongside fellow keeper Rajat Baghel.

**A familiar name, a different path.** Where Rahul Dravid spent 16 years building his reputation as the most dependable batsman in Test cricket — 13,288 runs at 52.31, 36 centuries — his son is only beginning. Anvay was part of a tri-series in late 2025 featuring two India U-19 sides and Afghanistan U-19, and his performances behind the stumps and with the bat were strong enough to earn a permanent place in the selectors' thinking.

https://x.com/BCCI/status/2064991473360318615

He is not the first Dravid to pull on India U-19 colours. His elder brother Samit, an all-rounder who has played for the Karnataka U-19 team and featured in the KSCA Maharaja Trophy for Mysuru Warriors, was also in the national conversation but could not break through. Samit made headlines last year when he played against Arjun Tendulkar — son of Rahul Dravid's long-time teammate Sachin — in a domestic match that felt like a generational echo of one of Indian cricket's great partnerships.

Yashbardhan Singh Chauhan will captain both squads on the tour. Lakshya Raichandani will serve as vice-captain. The tour begins in Hambantota on July 4 with the first one-day match, before moving to Galle for the first multi-day fixture on July 13 and Colombo for the second starting July 20.

**The broader context matters.** Indian cricket is in the middle of a generational shift. Virat Kohli is injured and may miss the England tour. Rohit Sharma, at 39, is playing what could be his last ODI series. The pipeline from U-19 to the senior team — the same pipeline that produced Kohli (U-19 World Cup 2008), Gill (2018), and Sooryavanshi (2026) — is more important than it has been in years.

For the diaspora, the Dravid name carries particular weight. Rahul Dravid's stint as India head coach, culminating in the T20 World Cup triumph, made him one of the most respected figures in the sport globally. NRIs who grew up watching The Wall block out sessions in Adelaide and Leeds will now track his son's progress with a mix of nostalgia and genuine curiosity.

No one is projecting Anvay into the senior squad. He is a teenager who has earned a place in a touring party. But in Indian cricket, where surnames carry the weight of expectation like nowhere else, the announcement is both a footnote and a headline.

**India U-19 ODI squad for Sri Lanka:** Yashbardhan Singh Chauhan (c), Lakshya Raichandani (vc), Rajat Baghel (wk), Anvay Dravid (wk), Sagar Virk, Vineeth VK, Arjun Rajput, Kushagra Ojha, Anmoljeet Singh, Vutkuri Yashveer Goud, Rohit Anil Yadav, Shavin V, Kavya Paresh Patel, Mohit Ulva, Ishan Sood.
